record.paper_title: Open Problems on Open Algebraic Varieties (Montreal 1994 Problems)
record.original_question: Let p be a polynomial in C[x1, ..., xn] such that the hypersurface X = {p = 0} in C^n is contractible. Must p be isotrivial, meaning that its generic fibers are pairwise isomorphic hypersurfaces in C^n?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$ and let $p \in \mathbb{C}[x_1, \ldots, x_n]$ be a polynomial such that the hypersurface $X = \{p = 0\} \subset \mathbb{C}^n$ is contractible (as a topological space). The polynomial $p$ is called isotrivial if there exists a Zariski open set $U \subset \mathbb{C}$ such that for all $c_1, c_2 \in U$, the fibers $\{p = c_1\}$ and $\{p = c_2\}$ are isomorphic as algebraic hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{C}^n$. 

Question: Must every such polynomial $p$, whose zero fiber is contractible, be isotrivial?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not turn up a definitive resolution of this question on isotriviality of polynomials with contractible zero fiber in $\mathbb{C}^n$. Related work on contractible affine varieties and on classifications of fibrations whose generic fiber is, e.g., a topological affine space, exists, but no clear affirmative or negative answer to the precise question was located. The status is therefore recorded as unknown.

status_evidence.title: Affine modifications and affine hypersurfaces with a very transitive automorphism group
status_evidence.snippet: Work on contractible affine hypersurfaces and their automorphism groups; does not resolve isotriviality of all contractible zero fibers.
status_evidence.claim: Related work on contractible affine hypersurfaces exists but does not directly settle the question.
